name: McCormick & Company, Incorporated

profile.description: McCormick is a global flavor company with two segments. Consumer sells spices, seasonings, condiments and hot sauces under McCormick, French's, Frank's RedHot, Lawry's, Cholula, OLD BAY, Ducros, Schwartz and Kamis. Flavor Solutions supplies seasonings and flavors to food manufacturers and restaurants. Fiscal Q3 2026 net sales rose 17.4% to $2.02B (organic +1.9%), helped by consolidating McCormick de Mexico, with adjusted EPS of $0.86. In March 2026 McCormick agreed to combine with Unilever's Foods business: about $20B of combined sales, Unilever shareholders owning 55%, and $15.7B of cash to Unilever, expected to close by mid-2027. Market cap is about $12.7B.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Under CEO Brendan Foley, McCormick has doubled the net sales contribution from innovation since 2022, built hot sauce (Frank's RedHot, Cholula) into a 'growth accelerator', and consolidated McCormick de Mexico, which added ~23 points of Consumer segment growth in Q3 2026 [1][5]. The pending Unilever Foods combination would be transformative, but it has not closed [2]. AI Deployment (2/2): McCormick began applying AI to flavor development with IBM Research in 2019, and Foley says AI and machine learning are now 'deeply integrated' from consumer insight through product development [5][6]. Market Share (2/2): The world's largest spice company, with category-leading brands [6]. Pipeline (1/2): The Unilever deal (close by mid-2027) and ongoing innovation are visible, but no named next-generation product launches with revenue targets were found [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D is not disclosed separately, so above-peer intensity cannot be verified [7].
innovation.label: STRONG

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): McCormick's purpose, 'To stand together for the future of flavor', is backed by a long-running Purpose-led Performance framework with published annual reports; the 2025 report, released June 5, 2026, states it hit its 2025 sustainability targets [8]. Community Impact (2/2): The Power of Giving program engaged ~60% of employees and donated nearly $11M to charities in 2024, with close to 8,500 employees taking part in 2025 [8]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found; the 96% individual-development-plan completion rate is not a retention metric [8]. Insider Buying (1/2): Director Gavin Hattersley bought 1,000 shares on the open market at $44.61 (~$44.6K) on October 2, 2026; other recent filings are phantom-stock awards [9].
inspiration.label: DEVELOPING

Forward P/E of 14.7 scores 1.00 [3]. Profit margin of 19.4% scores 0.97, which appears flattered by non-recurring items given the 8.6x trailing P/E versus $3.05-3.13 adjusted EPS guidance [1][3]. infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): McCormick makes physical flavor products (herbs, spices, seasonings, condiments and B2B flavor systems) grown, sourced, processed and distributed in the physical world. AI cannot substitute for these, and no analyst commentary found frames AI as a disruption risk [5]. AI is used as an enabler in flavor creation and consumer insight [5][6]. The real risks to the business (private label, consumer volume softness, GLP-1 diets) are not AI-driven. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI-derived revenue is reported; AI improves the innovation process rather than being sold [5].
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens McCormick is a mixed but leaning-infinite player. Its flavor-centric purpose and Purpose-led Performance reporting have been consistent for years, and the Unilever Foods combination is a bold bet on that cause: management is accepting minority (35%) ownership for current shareholders to build a global flavor company. Finite signals remain: Foley frames strategy around outcompeting private label and building a 'dominant flavor powerhouse', and integration of a business roughly twice McCormick's size is a major test of culture.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'To stand together for the future of flavor' is distinctive and visibly drives strategy, from the Unilever combination framed as creating a 'preeminent global flavor-focused company' to innovation priorities [2][8]. It has not clearly been tested by a costly sacrifice.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership chose a transformative combination that dilutes existing holders to ~35% and drew a ~6% share drop on announcement day, prioritizing long-term scale in flavor over near-term per-share optics [2]. The deal also carries finite logic (synergy targets, scale), so this is one courageous decision rather than a pattern.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership is stable (Foley will lead the combined company, which stays headquartered in Maryland), development plans reach 96% of employees, and wellness programs cover 100% [2][8]. No standout retention data was found, and a Chief Integration Officer role signals integration disruption ahead [9].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): McCormick has repeatedly reshaped its portfolio through acquisitions (French's, Frank's RedHot, Cholula, McCormick de Mexico consolidation) and is now pursuing the Unilever Foods combination. These moves deepen the core flavor identity rather than abandon a business model [1][2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Public framing centers on outcompeting private labels and building a 'dominant' flavor powerhouse, a win-oriented posture with no evidence of learning from specific rivals [5].

investment_thesis: McCormick offers category leadership at a depressed valuation. Shares at $47.29 trade at 14.7x forward earnings with a 4.1% yield and a 34% payout ratio, backed by dividends paid every year since at least 1986 and raised every year since at least 1999 [3]. Fiscal Q3 2026 showed operating leverage, with gross margin up 190bps and FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at 13-17% sales growth, 16-20% adjusted operating income growth and $3.05-3.13 adjusted EPS [1]. The Unilever Foods combination would create a ~$20B-revenue flavor-focused company, with reported run-rate cost synergies of $300M-$600M [1][2].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on the deal and organic growth. Organic growth was only 1.9% in Q3 (pricing +2.2%, volume -0.3%), and the five-year revenue CAGR is 4.1% [1][7]. The Unilever transaction requires $15.7B of cash to Unilever, will likely raise leverage well above today's 66% D/E, leaves current holders with ~35% of the company, and carries a long integration and regulatory timeline to mid-2027 [2]. Reported EPS fell to $0.36 from $0.84 on deal-related items [1]. Some Unilever investors are pressing for preservation of deforestation-free sourcing standards, which McCormick's current reporting does not explicitly commit to (Sustainalytics: medium risk) [4].
key_catalysts: Regulatory approvals and closing of the Unilever Foods combination by mid-2027, creating a ~$20B-revenue global flavor company
Delivery of FY2026 guidance (adjusted EPS $3.05-3.13, adjusted operating income +16-20%) as McCormick de Mexico consolidation and cost savings flow through
Gross margin expansion (+190bps in Q3) from cost savings and mix
Valuation re-rating from 14.7x forward P/E and a 4.1% yield if organic volumes recover
key_risks: Integration and leverage risk from absorbing a Unilever Foods business roughly twice McCormick's size and paying $15.7B in cash to Unilever
Weak organic volume (-0.3% volume/mix in Q3) amid private-label competition and cautious consumers
Dividend growth could slow after the deal as cash is redirected to deleveraging
ESG and sourcing scrutiny from Unilever investors over deforestation-free commitments, and Unilever's ~10% stake and four board seats affecting governance
